intro: Long before 1492, the Americas were home to great cities and empires. The Aztec built an island capital with floating gardens. The Maya carved the histories of their kings in stone and invented the zero. The Inca ran an empire along the Andes with roads, runners and knotted cords. Each society ranked people, from rulers and nobles down to commoners, and each asked the many to work for the few.

After 1492, Spain and Portugal built colonies that sorted people by birthplace and ancestry. Millions of Indigenous people died of disease and forced labor. About 12.5 million Africans were forced onto ships and carried into slavery. People inside these systems pushed back in many ways, from daily acts to the Haitian Revolution, until slavery was abolished across the Americas by 1888.

In this unit you will compare how these societies organized power and work. You will read primary sources and data with a careful eye. You will describe achievements and hard truths fairly. By the end, you will be able to explain how ranks were built, how people resisted them, and why their effects can still be seen.
bigQuestion: How did societies in the Americas rank people, and how did people resist and change those ranks?

timeline.t: The Classic period of Maya city-states begins
The Mexica found Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco
Pachacuti begins the rapid growth of the Inca Empire
Columbus, sailing for Spain, reaches the Caribbean
Spanish forces and their Indigenous allies take Tenochtitlan
Spain passes the New Laws to limit the encomienda
Portuguese forces destroy Palmares, a quilombo in Brazil
Miguel Cabrera paints a famous set of casta paintings
Enslaved people rise up in Saint-Domingue
The Thirteenth Amendment abolishes slavery in the United States
Brazil's Golden Law ends slavery, the last in the Americas

test.q: Where did the Mexica build their capital?
choices: On an island in Lake Texcoco
test.why: Tenochtitlan was founded around 1325 on an island in Lake Texcoco.
The pochteca were Aztec merchants organized in guilds.

test.q: Which achievement belongs to the Maya?
choices: A symbol for zero and a full glyph writing system
test.why: The Maya created glyph writing and a zero. Roads and quipu were Inca; chinampas were Aztec.

choices: An Andean group of related families who shared land and work
test.why: An ayllu was a kin group in the Andes that shared land, herds and work.

test.q: How did the Inca send messages quickly?
test.why: Chasqui runners passed messages along the roads in a relay. The Inca had no horses or carts.

test.q: Which statement is fair to the Aztec, Maya and Inca?
choices: They had no rulers or ranks
They had no achievements worth studying
They built great achievements and also had strict hierarchies
test.why: The unit asks readers to name both achievements and hard truths.

test.q: What did the Treaty of Tordesillas do?
choices: Divided expected lands between Spain and Portugal
test.why: In 1494 Spain and Portugal agreed on a line to divide lands in the Americas.

test.q: Who spoke out for Indigenous rights in the debate at Valladolid?
test.why: Las Casas argued that Indigenous people had rights. Sepulveda argued conquest was just.

test.q: What was a mestizo in colonial Spanish America?
choices: A person of Spanish and African ancestry
A person of Spanish and Indigenous ancestry
test.why: A mestizo had Spanish and Indigenous ancestry. Mulato meant Spanish and African ancestry.

test.q: Why do historians say casta labels were not truly fixed?
choices: Every label was chosen by the king
The same person could be recorded as different groups over time
test.why: Church records show one person listed as different groups, often as wealth changed.

test.q: About how many Africans were forced onto ships in the transatlantic slave trade?
test.why: SlaveVoyages estimates about 12.5 million embarked. About 400,000 went to mainland North America.

test.q: Why did planters in sugar colonies keep buying new captives?
choices: Harsh work killed so many that deaths outnumbered births
Laws banned children in the colonies
test.why: In many sugar colonies deaths outnumbered births, so planters kept buying captives.

choices: A quilombo of people who escaped slavery in Brazil
test.why: Palmares was a large quilombo in Brazil in the 1600s, led at the end by Zumbi.

test.q: Who led the Haitian Revolution until his capture in 1802?
test.why: Toussaint Louverture led until Napoleon's forces captured him. Dessalines declared independence in 1804.

test.q: Which country was the last in the Americas to abolish slavery?
test.why: Brazil ended slavery with the Golden Law of 1888.

write.prompt: Were the ranks of colonial society fixed, or could people change them? Use two or three facts or sources from this unit, such as the casta paintings, church records, Palmares or the Haitian Revolution, and explain your claim.
tips: State your claim in one clear sentence.
Name each source or fact you use and where it comes from.
Give the strongest point for the other side, then answer it.
Use unit terms like castas, criollo, maroons and abolition.
